title: ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE

alert.trigger: All engines are failed in flight.

effectivity.note: One version for all HS-TX: 280/0.77 optimum relight speed, windmill relight approaching or below FL 300.

summary: All engines fail: the captain side keeps PFD 1 and the left-seat pilot flies, in alternate law with no AP, FD or A/THR. The PM runs a short ECAM (RAT and emergency generator, 280/0.77, APU, idle, FAC 1 reset, glide range), then goes straight to the QRH ALL ENG FAIL. If fuel remains and the engines are not damaged, try windmill relights on both engines, then starter-assisted relights below FL 200. If nothing relights, the QRH continues to a forced landing or ditching: those sections are under From the manuals, not in the flow.

background.text: Thrust is lost so that level flight cannot be held. The alert may not trigger on a partial loss of thrust: the crew then decides between ALL ENG FAIL (time for a relight) and EMER LANDING (no time).
This alert inhibits ELEC EMER CONFIG. Its purpose is to secure RAT extension and emergency generator connection, then send the crew to the QRH.
All AC busbars are lost; the RAT supplies the emergency generator, which feeds AC ESS and DC ESS. Green and yellow hydraulics are lost; the RAT pressurizes blue.
Each APU start attempt takes about 3.5 min off the battery time; total battery time is more than 30 min.
The right aileron is lost and floats; the PF may use rudder trim to balance it instead of holding a stick input. It returns when the APU generator connects (ELAC 2).
Windmill relight is preferred: it works over a wide altitude range, tries all engines at once and does not depend on aircraft systems.

technique.text: The ECAM glide distance is an envelope value for a rough range estimate; the actual distance may differ.
Going faster than the optimum speed keeps relight conditions, but in alternate law there is no overspeed protection.
Prepare for a ditching or forced landing even if a runway can be reached, if no engine relights.
Forced landing: gear down by gravity even off a runway, to absorb energy. The brake accumulator allows a limited number of applications, and there is no anti-skid.
Ditching: DITCHING pb just before touchdown closes the valves under the aircraft; hold the pitch and keep the wings level until impact.

gaps.text: The title "ENG DUAL FAILURE - FUEL REMAINING" is not used in the supplied HS-TX manuals. They use ENG ALL ENGINES FAILURE (ECAM) and ALL ENG FAIL (QRH); the PDP shows a "FUEL REMAINING" title for the A330 only. Fuel remaining corresponds to the "relight can be attempted" branch here.
No source gives PF/PM turns for the QRH part. The order follows the QRH lines, with the FCTM and PDP notes; the 30 s masters timing is from the PDP slide.
The QRH lists CABIN CREW and PASSENGERS (PA) NOTIFY when no evacuation is needed; the company wording "REMAIN SEATED, RESUME NORMAL DUTIES" is noted on that line.
The handling flow stops at relight and STATUS. The no-relight, ditching and forced landing sections of the QRH are given only as verbatim procedures, without PF/PM turns.
HS-TO versions omitted (QRH 19.01A–B, 19.02B–19.03B and 19.05A blocks, FCOM P 41–43/226). The QRH points to 19.05A for a forced landing, but the HS-TX block starts on 19.05B.
